landscape.label: 2026 Price Guide
title: Kitchen Remodel
Pricing Guide
landscape.say: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Malibu in 2026? Here's the pricing guide: the three price tiers, what each one gets you, permit costs, and what makes a Malibu kitchen different.

landscape.label: 2026 Price Tiers
landscape.title: What a Malibu kitchen remodel costs
landscape.sub: 2026 ranges · depending on size and scope
landscape.say: In Malibu, a basic kitchen remodel runs about $45,000 to $55,000 and up. An in-depth kitchen makeover, the most popular scope, runs $55,000 to $75,000 and up. And a luxury kitchen runs $75,000 to $150,000 and up, depending on size and scope.

landscape.label: Tier 1 of 3
landscape.name: Basic kitchen remodel
landscape.desc: New paint, flooring, countertops & lighting with quality materials.

bullets.t: Ideal for a quick refresh or a rental

landscape.say: A basic kitchen remodel, at $45,000 to $55,000 and up, covers new paint, flooring, countertops, and lighting with quality materials. You'll usually keep your existing layout, with refaced or new stock cabinets and a new backsplash. It's ideal for a quick refresh or a rental property.

landscape.label: Tier 2 of 3
landscape.name: In-depth kitchen makeover
landscape.desc: Layout changes and higher-end materials throughout.
landscape.say: An in-depth kitchen makeover, $55,000 to $75,000 and up, is the most popular scope in Malibu. It adds layout changes and higher-end materials: new semi-custom cabinets, quartz or granite counters, a tile backsplash, appliance upgrades, and plumbing or electrical relocations.

landscape.label: Tier 3 of 3
landscape.name: Luxury kitchen
landscape.desc: Premium materials, custom everything, top-tier appliances.
landscape.say: A luxury kitchen, $75,000 to $150,000 and up, is the ultimate Malibu kitchen: a layout redesign and wall changes, custom cabinetry, full-slab quartz or granite, commercial-grade appliances, and a custom island or built-in seating.

landscape.label: What Drives the Price
landscape.title: What affects your kitchen price

cards.name: Size & layout
cards.desc: Bigger kitchens & layout changes cost more

cards.name: Cabinets
cards.desc: Refaced, stock, semi-custom or fully custom

cards.name: Countertops
cards.desc: Laminate, quartz, granite or full slab

cards.name: Plumbing & electrical
cards.desc: Moving a sink, range or outlets adds cost

landscape.say: So what moves your price? Your kitchen's size and layout, the quality of cabinets, your countertop material, appliance upgrades, any plumbing or electrical work, and your flooring and lighting choices.

landscape.label: Malibu Considerations
landscape.title: What makes Malibu different

cards.name: Coastal Commission
cards.desc: Interior remodels usually aren't reviewed; exterior or footprint changes may need a permit

cards.name: Ocean views
cards.desc: Open layouts that frame the Pacific

landscape.say: Malibu kitchens have a few extra considerations. Salt air corrodes standard hardware and appliances, so plan on marine-grade hardware and corrosion-resistant fixtures. An interior kitchen remodel usually doesn't need California Coastal Commission review, but changes to the exterior or footprint may need a coastal permit. And many Malibu remodels open up the layout to frame ocean views.

landscape.label: Permit Costs
landscape.title: Estimated permit costs
landscape.note: Estimates based on 2026 Southern California permit averages. Confirm with the City of Malibu.
landscape.say: Budget for permits too. A minor remodel with no layout changes runs about $420 to $735 in permit fees. Removing walls or upgrading plumbing or electrical, about $840 to $1,260. And a major remodel with structural changes, $1,260 to $1,575 and up. All Exclusive Construction handles permits with the City of Malibu for you.

landscape.label: Optional Upgrades
landscape.title: Upgrades that add cost
landscape.note: Prioritize the upgrades you'll use every day.
landscape.say: Optional upgrades add to the total: panel-ready appliances, custom storage like pantry pull-outs, slab backsplashes, heated floors, a beverage or coffee bar, and new windows, doors, or skylights.
